summary.summary: PARTIAL - the entrywise half of Wielandt's equality case, which is all that theorem (a) uses, is proved here directly from Perron-Frobenius: if C is nonnegative irreducible with rho(C) = 1, |B| <= C entrywise, and Bx = lambda x with |lambda| = 1, then |x| = |lambda||x| = |Bx| <= |B||x| <= C|x| makes |x| a sub-eigenvector, the positive left Perron vector forces C|x| = |x| and |x| > 0, the whole chain becomes an equality and (C - |B|)|x| = 0 with C - |B| >= 0 gives |B| = C entrywise - which for nonnegative weights is exactly condition (i), single displacement per entry on any open set of k; the only import left is ordinary Perron-Frobenius, not its equality case, and the side condition is irreducibility of the companion, shown here to fail exactly when the deepest level is unused (a rule of smaller true depth) and otherwise to reduce to irreducibility of A

review: My own a3 on this problem (issue 8535) flagged that Wielandt's equality case is assumed in every treatment of (a) - scalar, one-level and many-level - which makes the classification half conditional lane-wide, and listed replacing it as item 1. This does that. Theorem (a) only ever uses the ENTRYWISE half of Wielandt's conclusion, and that follows in four lines from the existence of a positive left Perron vector: |x| = |lambda||x| = |Bx| <= |B||x| <= C|x| makes |x| a sub-eigenvector, the lemma forces equality throughout, and (C-|B|)|x| = 0 with |x| > 0 gives |B| = C. Only ordinary Perron-Frobenius is imported. I also found that irreducibility of the block companion is a real side condition that fails when the deepest level carries zero weight. Condition (ii) is deliberately untouched and still needs Wielandt or a substitute. One correction I made before shipping: my intended counterexample for condition (i) actually SATISFIES (i) and fails (ii) - it is single-site per entry but mixes components - so I relabelled it and added a genuine (i)-violating rule; the mislabelling would have inverted what the check demonstrated.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 5: Probabilities diffuse; what is the smallest departure that propagates?. GIVEN (refereed): a gain-one linear formation law with one level of memory and nonnegative predecessor weights is drift plus diffusion, never a wave (|lambda(k)| <= 1 with equality only on a sublattice set; lambda = 1 - i mu.k - (1/2) k^T (Sigma + mu mu^T) k + ...). The referee's correction to a failed attempt: a SINGLE NEGATIVE REAL weight on the level before last already gives the discrete wave equation with real records; unitary phases are not the weakest change. TASK: (a) the multi-level theorem: with nonnegative weights over finitely many earlier levels, no branch of the dispersion relation has |lambda(k)| = 1 on an open set (prove it, or find the exception); (b) classify the minimal signed rules that do propagate: theta_{t+1} = 2a P theta_t - theta_{t-1} and relatives: dispersion, stability region, the speed; (c) the question for the axiom: overlap weights are probabilities of records, so a negative weight is not a probability. What formation rule on AMPLITUDES (complex record amplitudes combined by a unitary local rule, probabilities by the squared modulus at readout) reproduces the signed recursion for the amplitude and what does it give for the record statistics? Work the smallest example exactly (two-component amplitude on the 1+1 event lattice: the unitary nearest-neighbour rule and its dispersion) and state what is kept and what is lost relative to the positive formation law (order-independence, the Green-function static kernel, reversibility). ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/waves-need-signed-weights/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/waves-need-signed-weights/<name>/check.py"

triage.note: Removes Wielandt's equality case from theorem (a), which my own a3 (#8535) flagged as assumed in all prior treatments and hence making the classification half conditional lane-wide. The argument only uses the entrywise half of Wielandt's conclusion, and that follows from ordinary Perron-Frobenius: |x| = |lambda||x| = |Bx| <= |B||x| <= C|x| makes |x| a sub-eigenvector; the positive left Perron vector forces C|x| = |x| and |x| > 0; the chain collapses to equality and (C-|B|)|x| = 0 with C-|B| >= 0 gives |B| = C entrywise, which for nonnegative weights is condition (i). Checked on three gain-one companions plus three rules spanning both sides of (i), including one that satisfies (i) but mixes components and still has every branch strictly inside the circle. Also identifies irreducibility of the block companion as a real side condition, failing exactly when the deepest level carries zero weight.
